item.title: A Bit of Freedom Goes a Long Way: Classical and Quantum Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning under a Generative Model
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Andris Ambainis, Joao F. Doriguello, Debbie Lim
We propose novel classical and quantum online algorithms for learning finite- and infinite-horizon Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). Our algorithms are based on a hybrid online-offline reinforcement learning model wherein the agent can, from time to time, freely interact with the environment in a generative sampling fashion, i.e., by having access to a ''simulator''. By employing known classical and new quantum algorithms for approximating optimal policies under a generative model within our learning algorithms, we show that it is possible to avoid several paradigms from RL like ''optimism in the face of uncertainty'' and ''posterior sampling'' and instead compute and use optimal policies directly, which yields better regret bounds compared to previous works. item.title: Physics-informed distribution of relaxation times estimation and latent-space condition monitoring of solid oxide fuel and electrolysis cells from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Žan Gorenc, Žiga Gradišar, Felix Mütter, Vanja Subotić, Pavle Boškoski
arXiv:2608.13305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating the distribution of relaxation times (DRT) fromelectrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is an ill-posed inverse problem that is highly sensitive to regularisation choices. We propose a physics-informed convolutional autoencoder that estimates DRT directly from EIS data without spectrum-specific tuning. A discretised relation between impedance and the DRT is embedded in the training process, constraining the network to produce impedance-consistent distributions. The model resolves overlapping relaxation processes in synthetic two-ZARC spectra and accurately reconstructs measurements from three independent solid oxide fuel and electrolysis cell datasets, with range-normalised errors below 1.1%. arXiv:2608.12936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As quantum computing progresses from proof-of-principle demonstrations toward practical utility, a significant impediment is the need to augment algorithmic feasibility with system-level optimization across heterogeneous hardware and software stacks. item.title: A Unified Space–Time Finite Element Solution Framework for Electromagnetic–Mechanical Coupling Problems
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Wei Gu, Li Zhu, Yansong Guo, Shizhong Liang, Feng Wu, Xindi Wei
Electromagnetic–mechanical coupling problems are widely encountered in engineering applications. Traditional methods mostly adopt a solution paradigm that combines spatial finite element semi-discretization with temporal integration schemes. This paradigm may introduce numerical dissipation, energy drift, or fail to preserve the underlying symplectic structure during long-term transient simulations. To address these issues, this paper introduces a space–time finite element mesh and establishes a unified space–time discrete variational framework for electromagnetic–mechanical coupling problems, thereby avoiding the conventional treatment that separates spatial discretization from temporal integration. item.title: 受光子系统启发的束缚引力波
item.description:
📚 Physics News
人们通常将波理解为一种会传播的扰动，这适用于海岸波、空气中的声波以及通过光纤传输信息的电磁波。引力波同样是扰动，但它们作用于我们所处的时空这一具有弹性的结构，并在十年前首次被直接探测后进入公众视野。本文题目暗示研究借鉴光子系统来探索束缚引力波，具体理论与结果需查阅原文。

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Variational Quantum Feature Learning for Reliable High-Dimensional Classification
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Syed Basha Shaik, Srihari Varma Mantena, Shaik Janbhasha, V. Malsoru, Ravikiran Reddy Kandadi, RADHAKRISHNAN S 等7位作者
High-dimensional classification remains challenging for hybrid quantum–classical learning because conventional variational quantum feature learning methods often assign equal importance to all input features and do not explicitly account for feature uncertainty. This paper presents Uncertainty-Aware Variational Quantum Feature Learning (UVQFL), a hybrid framework that combines adaptive feature weighting, uncertainty estimation, and variational quantum representation learning for reliable classification. The proposed framework incorporates an Adaptive Feature Confidence Module (AFCM) to estimate the contribution of individual input features before quantum encoding and an Uncertainty Estimation Module (UEM) to characterize feature reliability during the learning process. item.title: Reasoning Jury: Multi-Model Consensus for Evaluating Reasoning Traces
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Congchao Wang, Diwakar Singh, Qiaozi Gao, Spyros Matsoukas, Yang Liu, Mahdi Namazifar
arXiv:2608.12585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Improving reasoning LLMs requires the ability to judge the quality of long reasoning traces for effective reasoning data curation, strong training signals during reinforcement learning, and an in-depth understanding of reasoning behaviors during model performance evaluation. Additionally, surfacing reasoning mistakes that the model makes would enable improving the model's performance at runtime through providing feedback. Due to the difficulty of this complex task on long reasoning traces, single-model judges (even frontier models) do not do well at identifying reasoning defects. item.title: 气候极端事件下华北平原玉米产量预测：一种作物模型与机器学习相结合的方法
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Haonan Tan, Dengpan Xiao, Huizi Bai, Yang Lu, Lihua Lv, Peipei Pan 等13位作者
基于过程的作物模型能够评估气候变化对产量的影响，但在描述极端气候事件造成的产量损失方面存在局限。本文将 APSIM 与随机森林、轻量梯度提升机相结合，并利用逐步回归和遗传算法筛选不同生育阶段的信息性极端气候指标。结果显示，APSIM+RF+GA 模型显著提高了产量预测精度，并预测在 SSP585₂₀₈₀ₛ 情景下，考虑二氧化碳施肥效应时春玉米和夏玉米产量损失分别为 25.0% 和 24.6%，不考虑时分别为 43.6% 和 26.8%。

item.title: Rules or Character? Scaling Laws for AI Safety Design
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Satoshi Takahashi, Nobuji Kouno, Masaaki Komatsu, Ryuji Hamamoto
arXiv:2608.13345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) safety systems combine character shaping (e.g., Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback [RLHF], Constitutional AI), which modifies behavioral distributions at training time, with rule enforcement (e.g., output filters, safety classifiers), which blocks harmful outputs at inference time, yet little formal analysis exists on how their optimal balance should change as deployment scales increase. item.title: Achieving Near 21% Efficiency Organic Solar Cells through Controlled Packing of Fused-Ring Electron Acceptors
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Nan Wei, Tong Sun, Hao Lu, Xiaodong Wang, Xueqing Ma, Jiahe Zhang 等15位作者
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76532-1 Non radiative energy loss remains a challenge in non-fullerene organic solar cells. Wei et al. introduce chlorobenzene-functionalized acceptors that exhibit enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield with a distinct molecular packing mode, enabling a power conversion efficiency of 20.92%.
